summary: The root WDY primarily means to pay blood-money or compensation for a life. It also refers to the act of giving or presenting something, often as a gift or offering.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: وَدَى القَتِيلَ He gave the bloodwit to the heir, or next of kin, of the slain person. (Msb.)
inf. n. مُوَادَاةٌ, He took [ from him ] the دِيَة. (TA.) See 3 in art. عدو.

أَوْدَى بِهِ It destroyed him; (T;) it removed him, or took him away: (M, K:) said of death [&c.]. (T, M, K.) See an ex. in art. بلو, conj. 8, and another voce أَزْلَمُ. أَوْدَى: see a verse cited voce قَلَبَةٌ. أَوْدَى العَيْرُ إِلّا ضَرِطًا: see ضَرَطَ.
Bloodwit; a fine for bloodshed, i. e., homicide; consisting of a hundred camels. دِيَاتُ جِرَاحَاتٍ [ Fines for wounds ]. (S, M, TA, &c., in art. شنق.)
Small فَسِيل, q. v.; (S, Msb, K;) shoots, or offsets, cut off from palm-trees and planted: (Mgh:) young palm-trees. (TA.)

[ A valley; a water-course, or torrent-bed: and sometimes a river; ] a space intervening, (M, Msb, K,) i. e. any such space, (M, Msb,) between mountains or hills; (M, Msb, K;) through which a torrent runs forth [ occasionally or constantly ]: (Msb:) for which reason it is thus called. (M, Mgh, TA.) حَلَّ بِوَادِيهِ i. q. بَاعَِ عَلَى بَيْعِهِ in one of the senses explained in art. بيع; i. e., (tropical:) He superseded him, &c.
; pl. تَوَادٍ, in the accus. case, by poetic licence, تَوَادِيًا: see a verse cited voce خُفٌّ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
